newsitem.title: CHINA: France, China sign space sciences exchange deal.
newsitem.headline: France, China sign space sciences exchange deal.

text.p: China and France on Tuesday signed an accord that will pave the way for scientific exchanges between the two nations' space industries, a French official said.
Chinese and French officials signed the deal, which is intended to lead to transfers of space research and information, an official with the French embassy said.

The signing was attended by a delegation led by the French minister for posts, telecommunications and space Francois Fillon and which included Francis Avanzi, director general of European space firm Arianespace, the official said.
China and France would not transfer space technologies under the accord in line with international treaties but would exchange research, information and teaching methods, she said.
The agreement, to be concluded when French President Jacques Chirac visits China in May, would cover exchanges of information on earth observation and satellite networks, she said.
The accord also called for such exchanges in the field of manned space flight preparation but Fillon had ruled out the idea of a joint Sino-European manned space mission, she said.
"They will help each other to master these technologies," she said.
The official said the accord, when completed, would also allow French and Chinese authorities to discuss using each other's rockets as back-ups in case of failure.

But Paris-based satellite launch company Arianespace said on Monday it was far from reaching a deal with Beijing to allow its Ariane rocket to be used as a back-up in case of failure of China's Long March launcher.
Fillon would leave Beijing on Wednesday to visit China's Xichang space centre in the southwestern province of Sichuan, she said, but gave no further details.
